top_signals.title: Tech Rally Loses Steam In Europe as Oil Rises
top_signals.summary:
A rally in technology stocks came to a halt as oil resumed its role in setting the tone for markets, with Brent heading for its first gain in a week as investors tracked diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war. Earlier, stocks got a lift after Meta’s new artificial intelligence agent, Muse, quickly rose to the top of mobile app charts.

The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Anna Edwards and Guy Johnson.

Correct: Graphic edited at 01;00;19;11, 01;27;09;02, 01;34;40;22 to clarify that Ermotti said fee pools in banking are going be down, with UBS in-line with market trends.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Ecuador Seeks US Help Fighting $30-Billion Cocaine Trade
top_signals.summary: Ecuador is asking the US "every day" for more help fighting a cocaine trade President Daniel Noboa estimates is worth $30 billion a year. In an interview with Bloomberg Television's Francine Lacqua in New York on Sept. 21, Noboa said Ecuador is "going after the big fish" and needs help from the US and Europe. He says about 1,200 tons of cocaine move through Ecuador each year, with roughly 80% destined for the US and Europe. But Noboa says Ecuador will remain in charge of all operations, saying the country would "never give a blank check to any country." (Source: Bloomberg)
